# Problem 1

I used simulation of groups of people to estimate the probability that at least two people share a birthday. Assuming that birthdays are independent and equal likely.

```{r}
has_shared_birthday = function(group_size) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = group_size, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(8105)

birthday_probabilities =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    simulation = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(shared_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, has_shared_birthday)) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(shared_birthday),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
birthday_probabilities |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a shared birthday",
    x = "Number of people",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
The estimated probability of a shared birthday increases with group size. It is approximately 50% for a group of 23 people.


## Problem 2

```{r}
library(readr)
```


```{r}
participant_data =
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
  mutate(data = purrr::map(path, read_csv)) |>
  unnest(data)

weekly_data =
  participant_data |>
  mutate(
    subject_id = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    arm = str_sub(subject_id, 1, 3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "outcome"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week)) |>
  select(subject_id, arm, week, outcome)
```
```{r}
weekly_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subject_id, color = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(~ arm) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly outcomes by study arm",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome",
    color = "Study arm"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
In the control arm, participants’ outcomes fluctuated from week to week with no clear trend. In the experimental arm, outcomes generally increased. By week 8, outcomes in the experimental arm are higher than those in the control arm.
